PFA alone can give “phantom” or “hyper-ChIP-able” peaks – signals that arise because open, highly transcribed chromatin is sticky and is pulled down even by unrelated antibodies.  
These artifactual peaks are concentrated at regions of maximal chromatin accessibility and transcription-factor occupancy, i.e. active promoters and enhancers.  
Adding the protein–protein cross-linker DSG allows more stringent washing and greatly reduces this nonspecific background, so those false peaks disappear.

Therefore the peaks that vanish after PFA + DSG fixation are most likely located at active promoters and enhancers.

Answer: D
